src/lib/deck-webgpu/device.ts.why: webgpuAvailable reason text names navigator.gpu (a string, no raw call); the adapter peek lives in gpu/adapter-peek.ts

src/lib/deck/composite.ts.why: WebGL2 fallback: MAX_SAMPLES probe, benchmark gl.finish, renderColorPixels RGBA/FLOAT readPixels, fence waits; MSAA is luma (rigi.5 multisampled textures + resolveTargets)

src/lib/deck/device-lost.ts.why: WebGL2 fallback: context-loss revival re-reads GL parameters and re-enables extensions on the restored context (luma has no restore API); private WebGLDevice members (_isLost, _resolveContextLost, _moduleData) are reset there too

src/lib/deck/geometry-pass.ts.why: WebGL2 fallback (no MSAA here): glFence/readbackQuiet probes, RED/FLOAT readability probe, the RGBA/FLOAT readPixels fallback (luma readBuffer reads only the texture's own format), copyRangeTo Y-flip blit (luma has no flipped blit); PBO pool retired in 888be38

src/lib/gpu/adapter-peek.ts.why: the one raw navigator.gpu.requestAdapter: adapter limits/features before device creation; @luma.gl/webgpu exports WebGPUAdapter as a type only and requestGPUAdapter is protected

src/lib/gpu/core/luma.ts.why: WebGPUAdapter.attach(handle: GPUDevice) wrapper for ORT / ownsHandle; the one sanctioned attach point (nativeWebGPUDevice / nativeWebGPUBuffer next to it hand ORT native objects)

src/lib/gpu/core/queue.ts.why: openErrorScopes: native push/popErrorScope for opt-in checks; luma WebGPUDevice.pushErrorScope/popErrorScope are no-ops unless the device was created with debug: true

src/lib/nearfield/deck-splat-layer.ts.why: WebGL2 splat layer on deck's gl context

src/lib/renderer-select.ts.why: engine probe: a probe requestDevice on the peeked adapter (+ the "no navigator.gpu" reason string); the one place that decides WebGPU vs WebGL2 and must not load the luma WebGPU chunk
